suggestions.title: Budgets assume someone already knows the price
suggestions.prompt: Three notes reach for the same metaphor without examining it: 'Context is a budget' (b), 'Attention is a budget too' (n7), 'Blast radius budgeting' (n14), with p-0807-1 saying the resemblance to money budgeting out loud. But a budget is allocated top-down by someone who already believes they know what each thing is worth. p-0721-1 (billing subagents for tokens) is the only mass on the other side — where scarcity is discovered rather than assigned. Unexplored: what an orchestrator learns when agents bid for context instead of being handed it, and whether the resulting prices are a better eval signal than any rubric.

suggestions.title: Decay as distance, not deletion
suggestions.prompt: The compaction and forgetting notes (k, n5) and p-0311-1 all treat memory loss as compression — something is dropped, the debate discarded, the verdict kept. But p-1101-1 (memory palaces for models) and p-1212-1 (the notebook should be a place, not a feed) point somewhere else: memory addressed by position, where old things get further away rather than deleted. No note asks what retrieval looks like when age is a coordinate instead of a filter — which is, quietly, the physics this map already runs on.
